results.name: Chest Press High to Low Cable Resistance Band
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a high anchor point behind you. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding a handle in each hand with your palms facing down.
Position one leg forward and the other back, with both knees slightly bent.Start with your elbows bent at 90 degrees and your hands at your chest sides.
Push the handles forward and down in a diagonal motion until your arms are fully extended and hands facing your hips.
Slowly return to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you push the handles forward and down, and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Keep your back straight and avoid using momentum.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Chest Press High to Low Cable Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Chest Press Low to High Resistance Band
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a low anchor point behind you. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding a handle in each hand with your palms facing down.
Position one leg forward and the other back, with both knees slightly bent. Start with your elbows bent and your hands close to your chest sides.
Push the handles forward and up in a diagonal motion until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly return to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you push the handles forward and down, and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Keep your back straight and avoid using momentum.
Focus on engaging your upper chest muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Chest Press Low to High Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Chest Press Machine
instructions: Sit down on the chest press machine with your feet flat on the floor and your back pressed firmly against the backrest. Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing forward, and position your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Push the handles forward and extend your arms fully, keeping a slight bend in your elbows to avoid locking them.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbows and bringing the handles back towards your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back and head flat against the backrest to maintain proper form.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you push the handles forward and inhale as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Chest Press Machine is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Chest Tap Push Up
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your chest is just above the floor, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Explosively push through your palms to lift your body back up, lifting both hands off the floor at the top of the movement.
While in the air, tap your chest with both hands, then quickly place your hands back on the floor and repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement with control, especially when lowering your body, to prevent injury.
Keep your feet slightly wider apart to enhance stability during the explosive push-up and chest tap.
Focus on a strong, explosive push to lift your body and hands off the floor for the chest tap.
results.description: Chest Tap Push Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Upper Back.

results.name: Clap Push Ups
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your chest is just above the floor, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Explosively push through your palms to lift your body off the floor. While in the air, quickly clap your hands together in front of your chest.
Place your hands back on the floor to catch yourself and immediately lower into the next push-up. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your chest, shoulders, and triceps to generate the explosive power needed to lift your body off the floor.
Perform the movement with control, especially when landing, to avoid jarring your wrists and shoulders.
Start with regular push-ups to build strength before progressing to clap push-ups if needed.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you push up and clap, and inhaling as you lower yourself.
results.description: Clap Push Ups is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Core, Upper Back.

results.name: Climber a Padded Stool Supported
instructions: Begin in a plank position on the floor with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. The padded stool should be in front of you.
Engage your core and place your right hand on the stool, followed by your left hand, lifting your upper body onto the stool.
Reverse the movement by placing your right hand back on the floor, followed by your left hand, lowering your body back into the plank position.
Continue climbing up and down the stool, alternating which hand leads the movement for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
tips: Focus on controlled movements, ensuring you have a stable grip on the stool to avoid slipping.
Use a stable stool or bench to support your hands and ensure it is placed on a non-slip surface to prevent movement.
Ensure your shoulders remain directly over your hands to avoid unnecessary strain on your wrists and shoulders.
results.description: Climber a Padded Stool Supported is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Triceps.

results.name: Clock Push Ups
instructions: Begin in a standard push-up position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Perform a push-up by lowering your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, then push back up to the starting position.
Move your right hand and left hand a few inches to the left (clockwise) and perform another push-up.

Return both hands to the starting position and perform another push-up. Repeat this sequence, alternating between the starting position and the clockwise position for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
tips: Focus on maintaining proper form during each push-up, ensuring your elbows are at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Perform the movement with control, especially when moving your hands, to avoid unnecessary strain on your wrists and shoulders.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower yourself.
results.description: Clock Push Ups is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Close Grip Push Up
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed under your shoulders, with straight arms. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Push through your palms to lift your body back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your triceps and chest muscles to lift your body, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Perform the movement with control, especially during the lowering phase, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower yourself.
results.description: Close Grip Push Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Decline Kneeling Push Up on Box
instructions: Begin by placing your knees on a box and position your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart.
Engage your chest and ensure your body forms a straight line from your head to your knees.
Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Push through your hands to return to the starting position, straightening your arms. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid flaring your elbows out to the sides; keep them at a 45-degree angle to engage your chest and triceps more effectively.
Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
results.description: Decline Kneeling Push Up on Box is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Decline Kneeling Push Up
instructions: Begin by placing your knees on a step up and position your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart.
Engage your chest and ensure your body forms a straight line from your head to your knees.
Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Push through your hands to return to the starting position, straightening your arms. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid flaring your elbows out to the sides; keep them at a 45-degree angle to engage your chest and triceps more effectively.
Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
results.description: Decline Kneeling Push Up is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.
